title: Telemetry surface-area hardening: redaction, retention, and audit playbook
creator: Aditi Mehra
description: Goal: Reduce telemetry exposure by codifying a playbook that hardens the surface area across traces, logs, and metrics pipelines. This ticket scopes standardized redaction transforms for trace/span attributes and log lines, retention tiering for metrics/logs/traces, and an immutable audit trail for access and unmasking operations. Deliverables: (1) transform library for tracing hooks and log processors, (2) retention policy engine config and rollout plan, (3) RBAC + access-logging design for observability UIs and read APIs, (4) runbook for incident-safe just-in-time unmasking and post-unmask audit. This effort ties into Console rollout (per-route telemetry controls) and Dedicated privacy contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hook library implemented and enabled in staging: attribute-level scrub rules plus allowlist/denylist support
Log pipeline has deployable redact stage with configurable rules per-tenant and per-pipeline
Retention tiers defined and enforced for traces, logs, metrics with migration path for existing data
Access audit produced for every read/unmask event and surfaced to Console audit view
Automated tests for redaction correctness and a small benchmark showing <5% median latency impact for agent-side scrubbing
Runbook exists and has been exercised in a tabletop for one recent incident replay
tasks: Design: finalize attribute classification taxonomy and tenant-scoped default policies
Engineering: implement tracing hook adapter (OpenTelemetry -> Redwood scrub API)
Engineering: add redact transform to log ingestion (vector/ingest pipeline) and enable feature flag
Infra: retention-engine config and migration script for hot->warm->cold tiers
Security: define RBAC roles for observability consoles and grant review flow
QA: build fuzz tests for redaction edge cases (unicode, binary blobs, structured JSON)
Docs: Confluence playbook + Console help text for telemetry controls
Rollout: staged rollout plan (canary tenants -> orgs -> global) and rollback criteria
